findings.title: DNS records pointing to hostnames have valid targets without takeover risk
findings.detail: MX record danibarranquero.com points to potentially dangling target . - potential mail interception risk.
findings.risk: Dangling **DNS records** pointing to non-existent targets create multiple vulnerabilities. Dangling CNAME/NS allows **subdomain takeover**; dangling MX allows **mail interception**. Attackers can impersonate your organization, hijack services, or redirect legitimate traffic to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
findings.remediation:
Remove or update **dangling DNS records** to prevent takeover and interception attacks.
- Regularly audit DNS records when decommissioning services
- Remove CNAME, MX, NS, and SRV records pointing to deprovisioned resources
- Monitor for unauthorized changes to DNS records
- Consider using DNS monitoring tools to detect dangling records

disposition.note: A false positive, and acting on it would make things worse. The flagged target is the null MX from RFC 7505: an MX record pointing at "." is the standard way to declare that a domain receives no mail at all. The check reads that "." as a dangling hostname and warns about mail interception, which is precisely what the null MX prevents. Removing the record to turn this green would reopen the risk it is warning about.

findings.title: DNS records do not expose internal IP addresses
findings.detail: DNS record danibarranquero.com (AAAA) exposes internal IP address 100:: - information disclosure risk.
findings.risk:
DNS records exposing **internal IP addresses** leak sensitive network information.
- **Confidentiality**: reveals internal network topology and addressing schemes to attackers
- **Integrity**: provides reconnaissance data for targeted attacks on internal infrastructure
- **Availability**: internal IPs in public DNS may indicate misconfiguration affecting service routing
findings.remediation:
Remove **internal IP addresses** from public DNS records.
- Use split-horizon DNS for internal service resolution
- Ensure DNS records only contain publicly routable IP addresses
- Review DNS records after network changes or migrations
- Consider using Cloudflare Access for secure internal service access

disposition.note: A false positive, and worth stating plainly. The address is 100::, the IPv6 discard prefix from RFC 6666, which is what Cloudflare writes for a record that exists only to be proxied. It is not an internal address and it never leaves the account: externally the zone answers with Cloudflare anycast addresses, and a public AAAA lookup returns 2606:4700 addresses, never this one.

findings.title: Rate limiting is configured for the zone
findings.detail: No rate limiting rules configured for zone danibarranquero.com.
findings.risk:
Without **Rate Limiting**, applications are vulnerable to volumetric attacks.
- **Confidentiality**: credential brute forcing can compromise user accounts
- **Integrity**: API abuse can manipulate data through excessive requests
- **Availability**: volumetric attacks can exhaust resources causing service degradation
findings.remediation:
Implement **Rate Limiting** as part of defense in depth.
- Configure thresholds based on expected traffic patterns
- Apply stricter limits to sensitive endpoints like authentication and APIs
- Use different rate limits for different paths or endpoints
- Monitor rate limiting analytics to fine-tune thresholds

disposition.note: Available on the free plan, which allows one rule, so this is a choice rather than a limit. Rate limiting protects an origin from being overwhelmed, and there is no origin: every response is a static asset served from Cloudflare edge cache on unmetered bandwidth. The only free action is a challenge, which would put an interstitial in front of real readers to defend against nothing.

findings.title: WAF is enabled
findings.detail: WAF is not enabled for zone danibarranquero.com. This may be expected because the Web Application Firewall is not available on the Cloudflare Free plan.
findings.risk:

- **Integrity**: XSS attacks can modify page content and steal session tokens
- **Availability**: application-layer attacks can cause service disruption

- Create custom rules based on your application's specific threat model
- Monitor WAF analytics to tune rules and reduce false positives
- Combine with rate limiting and bot protection for comprehensive security

disposition.note: The Web Application Firewall is not available on the Cloudflare free plan. Prowler says so itself in the finding. The site is static files with no origin server, no database and no user input, so the attack classes a WAF blocks have nothing here to reach.

findings.detail: Bot Fight Mode is not enabled for zone danibarranquero.com.

- **Integrity**: credential stuffing attacks can compromise user accounts
- **Availability**: bot traffic can overwhelm resources causing service degradation

Enable **Bot Fight Mode** as part of a layered bot management strategy.

- Protects against web scraping and credential stuffing
- Combine with rate limiting and WAF rules for comprehensive protection

disposition.note: Mutually exclusive with the Content-Security-Policy on this site. Bot Fight Mode injects an inline challenge script whose r and t parameters change on every request, so no hash and no nonce can ever match it. Turning it on would mean adding unsafe-inline to script-src. Trading a real CSP for bot noise on a static site with no login and no forms is the wrong way round.

findings.title: Cloudflare Zone Firewall Rules Use Blocking Actions to Protect Against Threats
findings.detail: Zone danibarranquero.com has no firewall rules with blocking actions.
findings.risk:
Firewall rules configured only for **logging** provide visibility but no protection.
- **Confidentiality**: malicious traffic can access and exfiltrate sensitive data
- **Integrity**: application exploits can modify data without being blocked
- **Availability**: credential stuffing and abuse attacks reach the origin unimpeded
findings.remediation:
Configure **firewall rules** with blocking actions to enforce security policies.
- Use challenge actions for suspicious traffic to verify human visitors
- Use block actions for known malicious patterns and high-risk sources
- Test rules in log mode before enabling blocking to avoid false positives
- Follow the principle of least privilege in rule configuration

disposition.note: Custom firewall rules are available on the free plan. Nothing here is worth blocking: the entire site is public static content meant to be read, there is no authenticated surface, and no path that changes state. A blocking rule written only to satisfy a check would be configuration theatre.

findings.title: DKIM record exists with valid public key
findings.detail: DKIM record exists for zone danibarranquero.com but has invalid or missing public key: *._domainkey.danibarranquero.com.
findings.risk: Without **DKIM** or with a revoked/empty public key, recipients cannot verify messages were sent by authorized servers. Attackers can forge emails from your domain, and content integrity cannot be proven. DMARC policies relying on DKIM will fail, affecting deliverability. A DKIM record with empty `p=` indicates a revoked key.
findings.remediation:
Configure **DKIM records** with valid public keys from your email provider.
- Each email service requires its own DKIM selector (e.g., google._domainkey for Google Workspace)
- The `p=` parameter must contain the actual public key, not be empty
- An empty `p=` value indicates a revoked key and will fail this check
- DKIM works alongside SPF and DMARC for comprehensive email authentication
- Rotate DKIM keys periodically for enhanced security
- Use 2048-bit keys for stronger cryptographic protection

disposition.note: This domain sends no mail, so there is no key to publish. The record is *._domainkey with an empty p=, which RFC 6376 defines as a revoked key, and alongside SPF -all, DMARC p=reject and a null MX it is the recommended way to say "nothing here signs mail". The check looks for a valid public key and finds none, which is correct and also the point.

findings.title: HSTS is enabled with recommended max-age and includes subdomains
findings.detail: HSTS is enabled for zone danibarranquero.com with max-age of 31536000 seconds and includes subdomains.
findings.risk:

- **Integrity**: first request can be intercepted and modified before HTTPS redirect
- **Session hijacking**: cookies and credentials may be captured during initial HTTP request
findings.remediation:
Enable **HSTS** with at least a **6-month max-age** (12 months recommended).
- Verify all resources work over HTTPS before enabling
- Enable **include_subdomains** to protect all subdomains
- Consider **HSTS preloading** for maximum protection against SSL stripping attacks
- Test thoroughly as HSTS cannot be easily disabled once deployed

- **Compliance**: TLS 1.0/1.1 are deprecated by PCI-DSS, NIST, and major browsers
- **Integrity**: downgrade attacks can force weaker encryption that is susceptible to tampering
findings.remediation:
Set **minimum TLS version** to `1.2` or higher.
- **TLS 1.0 and 1.1** are deprecated by all major browsers and contain known vulnerabilities
- Consider setting to `TLS 1.3` for environments with modern client requirements
- Test client compatibility before upgrading minimum version

findings.title: DNS records do not use wildcard entries

- If wildcards are required, ensure the target service handles unknown subdomains securely
- Document the business justification for any wildcard records
- Combine with proper web server configuration to reject unknown hosts

findings.title: DMARC record exists with enforcement policy (p=reject or p=quarantine)
findings.detail: DMARC record with enforcement policy p=reject exists for zone danibarranquero.com: _dmarc.danibarranquero.com.
findings.risk: Without **DMARC** or with `p=none`, there is no active protection against email spoofing. Attackers can spoof emails for **phishing campaigns** to steal credentials. Domain reputation is damaged by spoofed emails. The `p=none` policy only generates reports but does not block or quarantine spoofed emails.
findings.remediation:
Implement **DMARC** with an enforcement policy (`p=reject` or `p=quarantine`).
- `p=reject`: receiving servers should reject emails that fail authentication
- `p=quarantine`: receiving servers should send suspicious emails to spam folder
- `p=none`: only monitoring, provides no protection (will fail this check)
- Ensure SPF and DKIM are properly configured before enabling enforcement
- Configure `rua` to receive aggregate reports on authentication results
- Use `pct` parameter to gradually roll out enforcement (e.g., `pct=10` for 10% of emails)

findings.title: SPF record exists with strict policy (-all)
findings.detail: SPF record with strict policy -all exists for zone danibarranquero.com: danibarranquero.com.
findings.risk: Without **SPF** or with a permissive policy (`~all`, `?all`, `+all`), attackers can forge emails from your domain. Phishing attacks can harvest sensitive information from recipients who trust spoofed emails. Brand reputation is damaged by fraudulent emails. `~all` only marks emails as suspicious without rejecting them.
findings.remediation:
Configure **SPF records** with strict policy (`-all`) listing authorized mail servers.
- SPF records start with `v=spf1` and define authorized senders
- Use `-all` (hardfail) to reject emails from unauthorized servers
- Avoid `~all` (softfail) in production as it only marks suspicious emails but does not reject them
- Use `include:` to authorize third-party mail services
- Combine with **DKIM** and **DMARC** for comprehensive email authentication
- Test SPF records using online validators before deployment

findings.title: TLS 1.3 is enabled

Enable **TLS 1.3** to provide the most secure and efficient TLS connections.
- All modern browsers support TLS 1.3 ensuring broad compatibility
- TLS 1.3 removes obsolete cryptographic algorithms
- Zero round-trip time (0-RTT) resumption improves performance
- Combine with minimum TLS version set to 1.2 or higher

findings.title: Cloudflare Zone Challenge Passage Is Configured Between 15 and 45 Minutes

- The default Cloudflare value of 30 minutes is recommended for most use cases
- Adjust based on your specific threat model and user experience requirements

findings.title: CAA record exists with issue or issuewild tag
findings.detail: CAA record with certificate issuance restrictions exists for zone danibarranquero.com: danibarranquero.com, danibarranquero.com, danibarranquero.com.
findings.risk: Without **CAA** records or `issue`/`issuewild` tags, any certificate authority can issue certificates for your domain. Unauthorized certificates enable **man-in-the-middle attacks** and domain impersonation. CAA records with only `iodef` tags do not restrict certificate issuance.
findings.remediation:
Add **CAA records** with `issue` or `issuewild` tags specifying authorized certificate authorities.
- `issue` tag: authorizes CAs for regular (non-wildcard) certificates
- `issuewild` tag: authorizes CAs for wildcard certificates specifically
- Use `issue ";"` to block all certificate issuance (for domains that should never have certificates)
- Use `iodef` tag to receive reports of policy violations (optional, for monitoring)
- All CAs are required to check CAA records before issuing certificates

findings.title: Under Attack Mode is disabled during normal operations
findings.detail: Zone danibarranquero.com does not have Under Attack Mode enabled.
findings.risk:
Keeping **Under Attack Mode** permanently enabled causes operational issues.
- **Availability**: all visitors face a 5-second interstitial challenge page before accessing the site
- **Accessibility**: visitors without JavaScript support cannot access the site at all
- **User Experience**: legitimate users experience unnecessary delays and third-party analytics show degraded performance
findings.remediation:
Disable **Under Attack Mode** when not actively under a DDoS attack.
- Use it only as a **last resort** during active layer 7 DDoS attacks
- For ongoing protection, use **Security Level** settings (Low, Medium, High)
- Configure specific **WAF rules** for targeted protection without impacting all users
